items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: bass was Al McKibbon (a very good friend of ours, right?)

ctx.x: Yeah, we had some very fine players with the band. In the trumpet section we had Edwin Davis (they called him Youngblood), and the other trumpet was Ducky Taylor. And on trombone we had the great Trombone Smitty, the legend from around Detroit. And Stack Walton on one tenor, Lorenzo Lawson playing the other tenor, and I was playing alto in the middle. And on drums we had Amos Woodard, and bass was Al McKibbon (a very good friend of ours, right?). And Johnny Martin was the pianist, and he was also one of the…

And Maurice King was writing for some of the shows, some of the acts that we had to play behind. Now, Maurice King, he's now the musical director for Motown Records; in fact, he's been for a long time the music director over there. And he was a great alto saxophone player himself.
